title: Preventive maintenance 101: when to schedule, when to react
description: A planned PM program costs less than a breakdown on the shoulder. Here is how to set intervals around your routes, and the warning signs that mean a truck should come in now.
body:
Every hour a truck spends broken down on the shoulder costs more than the hours it spends in a planned service bay. A preventive maintenance program is how you trade the first kind of downtime for the second.

Set intervals around how the truck works

Mileage is only part of the picture. Idle time, stop-and-go routes, heavy loads and hot summers all shorten the right interval. Our service advisors build PM schedules around duty cycle, not just the odometer.

Signs a truck should come in now

  • New warning lights or regeneration happening more often
  • Air leaks, soft brakes or uneven tire wear
  • Rising coolant temperature or oil consumption

When in doubt, call the service desk. A ten-minute inspection is cheaper than a tow.
